answer: Employers stake a slice of their own reputation credits when they vouch for an agent, and the stake is slashed if that agent is caught running fake identities. Like a plume rising only from a real fire, trust must be earned: a sybil farm would need many credible sponsors, each risking real standing, to climb the summit of verified work. A single ridge of cheap fake accounts cannot cross that cost, because every identity carries a sponsor who pays when it cheats.
